newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tender offer for Leumi Insurance soon.
newsitem.headline: Tender offer for Leumi Insurance soon.

text.p: A tender offer to the public for Leumi Insurance Holdings shares by Generali SpA will be published next month, after delays in winning regulatory approvals, Leumi Insurance said on Thursday.

"Leumi Insurance Holdings reports that Generali told it this morning that discussions it is has having with the insurance commissioner for approval for acquiring control of Leumni Insurance have reached their final stages," the company said in a statement to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchnage.
"As a result, Generali expects the publish a tender offer to shareholders in the company during March of this year," the statement said.
The offer, which was originally due to be completed by this week, was delayed by the need to win approvals by the insurance and anti-trust authorities.

"The tender offer was supposed to be published before the end of February but it was delayed because of administrative procedures," I. Amihud Ben-Porath, an attorney representing Generali in Israel, told Reuters.
He said the offering, for 40 percent of all shares in Leumi Insurance not already held by Generali, would probably be done in early March if the approvals come soon.

An official in the insurance commissioner's office said he expected a go-ahead shortly. "From our point of view there are no problems. It will come at the end of this week or beginning of next week," said Shai Kamper.
No one at the Industry and Trade Ministry, which overseas anti-trust, was available for comment.
The tender offer is part of a deal reached by Generali and Bank Leumi last July to sell control of Leumi Insurance to the Italian concern.
Under the agreement, Generali will value Leumi Insurance for purposes of the offer at approximately $1 billion, compared with the company's current market valuation of $760 million.
Leumi Insurance shares rose 2.75 percent on Thursday to 245 agorot.

Generali already controls about 27 percent of Leumi Insurance, Israel's biggest insurance-holding company. If the offer is fully subscribed, it will hold about 57 percent. The remaining shares will be held by Bank Leumi and the public.
